method: Read every assigned body in full from family.packet.json before consulting initial_survey.json, recording all retained body paragraphs. Compared the family texts with the survey and cross-group source packet; quotations were checked as exact substrings of the cited packet paragraph.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Initiates a Herbert exchange from Osmaston/Derby context: asks for specifically located beetles, reports collecting and the Foxes' music meeting, and requests a long account of Herbert's proceedings. The promise to write and requests for a future account do not identify an earlier Herbert letter.

Explicitly answers a Herbert letter received only a few days earlier after a forwarding mistake, and says Butler supplied an account of the Welsh proceedings. It separately narrates two Whitley admonitions and Darwin's intervening humble answer; neither Whitley input is the Herbert letter.

proposed_links.reason: Darwin says, "Very many thanks for your letter. owing to a mistake of not forwarding it, I only received a few days ago" (DCP-LETT-49 P1). Exact incoming identity and receipt date remain unlocated.

Darwin distinguishes the first letter ("When I arrived home, I received such a letter from old Whitley") and a later response ("merely received an acknowledgement of my extreme candour, another charge of the same description as before") (P1).

outgoing_reviews.summary: A dated mock petition to the family for a £20 replacement double-barrelled gun, ending in a four-person subscription list. It is a self-contained request and supplies no incoming prompt.

Darwin writes on Susan's third sheet to Erasmus, apologizing for estrangement and reporting Cambridge rooms, prints, Fox, entomology, and friends. The packet explicitly identifies this as Darwin's contribution to Susan's sheet; no incoming Erasmus letter is named.

Initiates Caroline correspondence for Shropshire politics and gossip, while describing Cambridge, Henslow's lecture and geology help, Humboldt, Spanish, and tropical plans. The request for an answer is prospective.

Reports the expedition possibility through Wood, Henslow, Peacock, and partial knowledge of FitzRoy's letter, then asks Susan to inspect a held Henslow letter and locate books, bills, funds, and directions. The physical Henslow letter is held at home and Darwin does not say he read it; the Captain's letter is known only in part through Wood.

corrections.reason: The survey's candidate 105 remains only a candidate: "Do not forward Henslows letter. you may open it, if you like" (DCP-LETT-115 P4) attests possession and a possible future reading by Susan, not Darwin's reading.

proposed_links.reason: DCP-LETT-115 P4 refers to a held Henslow letter, but no wording identifies it as DCP-LETT-105 or proves Darwin read it. P1 instead says he heard only a part of FitzRoy's letter through Wood.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Reworks the previous day's family account after Wood received FitzRoy's discouraging letter and Darwin met FitzRoy. It gives detailed terms, ship arrangements, costs, and route, but the third-party FitzRoy-to-Wood letter remains oral/partial context.

corrections.reason: "bringing up the other with me & altering it" (DCP-LETT-117 P1) supports a revision or continuation of 115's draft/account, but does not establish that 115 was posted, received, or read by Susan.

proposed_links.reason: The explicit "bringing up the other with me & altering it" (P1) points to an earlier account, and chronology makes 115 the natural candidate; dispatch and receipt are unproved.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Adds equipment and medical commissions, describes FitzRoy's advice and the proposed route, and says the voyage is not settled. The phrase "since I received the letter" does not identify whether 105, 106, or their bundled forwarding is meant; a request to write and receive an answer is future-facing.

proposed_links.reason: "since I received the letter" (DCP-LETT-119 P2) is too nonspecific to distinguish Henslow's and Peacock's communications or prove full reading; P1 asks whether there is time to write and receive an answer before departure.

outgoing_reviews.summary: A long same-day/update account covering a received parcel, Beaufort/FitzRoy arrangements, coronation observations, purchases, and route. The parcel is not a letter; "my letter written next day" likely points to 119 but is not uniquely identified, and the hoped-for letter from Susan is not receipt evidence.

proposed_links.reason: "you have received my letter written next day" (DCP-LETT-122 P1) likely refers to the 6 September equipment letter 119, but the relative wording does not itself prove unique identity.
"I have just received the parcel" (P1) identifies a physical parcel, not an incoming letter or textual prompt.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Reports the three-day journey to Plymouth, the Beagle, FitzRoy, officers, delayed sailing, funds, and fluctuating confidence. References to former letters and money at the bank do not identify an incoming family text.

Updates Susan after cabins are assigned: Darwin now regards the voyage as fixed, explains his cabin and companion, arms, survey aims, and travel dates. It refers back to a Plymouth letter and announces a future Maer letter; neither creates a new incoming family target.

proposed_links.reason: "you have received my letter from Plymouth" (DCP-LETT-127 P1) fits 126's Plymouth account, but the relative reference is not independently unique.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Answers a Caroline letter and separately acknowledges a Catherine letter, then discusses the tutor/furniture bill, living arrangements, and delayed sailing. It also says an unlocated letter to Susan was written the same day and recalls an earlier letter to Mr Ash. Date remains questioned as 31? October.

proposed_links.reason: "I received your letter the same day that I wrote to Susan" (DCP-LETT-145 P1) explicitly attests a Caroline incoming and a separate same-day outgoing to Susan, without recovering either calendar date.
"Since which I have had one from Katty" (P1) establishes a separate Catherine input after the Caroline letter; no direct reply is stated.

outgoing_reviews.summary: Updates Caroline on the tutor bill, Beagle fitting, social visits, sea-sickness, route, and correspondence logistics. The tutor-bill knowledge does not prove a new Caroline letter; "since Susan's date" establishes an earlier Susan-dated communication but not its identity or contents.

proposed_links.reason: "I suppose you have received a letter from me since Susan's date" (DCP-LETT-146 P6) refers to Susan's dated communication and Darwin's own letter, but does not recover the Susan letter's date or prove a direct response.
The bill is "just as I expected" (P1), but that could derive from prior knowledge or another channel; no new Caroline letter is explicitly acknowledged.

incoming_reviews.summary: Fanny apologizes for delaying a note, reports Brighton parties, asks for Shrewsbury scandal, and requests mysteries; it is social correspondence with no surviving Darwin reply identified in this family set.
unlocated_references: The delayed Darwin note/previous entertaining budgets are referred to but not identified as a surviving outgoing or incoming record.

incoming_reviews.summary: Fanny explains that Cambridge and Mrs Burton's propriety fears delayed her reply, then discusses the Woodhouse travels, Bazaar, balls, and riding. No direct Darwin target survives in this family packet.
unlocated_references: The agreeable Darwin letter that prompted this answer is not identified.

incoming_reviews.summary: Sarah answers Darwin's Brighton effusion with a long social report: fancy ball, London visits, Forest gossip, family marriage rumors, horses, and an explicit request for his opinion. No surviving direct Darwin reply is assigned here.
unlocated_references: Sarah's referenced agreeable effusion from Darwin and the earlier promise to write are not uniquely identified.

incoming_reviews.summary: Fanny apologizes for delayed response, reports parties, family visitors, riding, Cambridge, and asks when Darwin will come home. It supplies no surviving direct Darwin reply in this packet.
unlocated_references: The long Darwin effusion to which Fanny responds is not identified.

incoming_reviews.summary: Sarah says Catherine dispatched a substantial letter addressed to Darwin and therefore delayed writing; she supplies Forest gossip, rumors, marriages, horses, and an invitation to continue. This explicitly attests Catherine's outgoing dispatch, but not Darwin's receipt or reading of it.
unlocated_references: A "very considerable dispatch composed by Catherine & directed to Mr. Charles Darwin" is attested (P1), but no receipt, reading, or surviving target is established.

proposed_links.reason: Sarah witnessed the departure of the dispatch (P1), but witnessing its posting does not establish Darwin's receipt or reading.

incoming_reviews.summary: Fanny requests Darwin's account of Forest/Bliss/Darwin-Hall mysteries and discusses the sale, bachelors, and family gossip. No direct Darwin reply is assigned in this family set.
unlocated_references: The prior Darwin communications and any answer to Fanny are not identified.

incoming_reviews.summary: Fanny thanks Darwin for books and a swallow-tail, reports Oswestry theatre, family visits, painting, riding and billiards, and says she has forgotten the note's purpose. No direct reply is preserved here.
unlocated_references: Darwin's long dispatch and the books/swallow-tail delivery channel are referenced, but no unique incoming or reply pairing follows.

incoming_reviews.summary: Fanny answers Darwin's request for a letter with Hunt-week, Forest, Clare's singing, beetle jokes, the Williams uncertainty, finances, and family news. No direct Darwin reply survives in this assignment.
unlocated_references: Darwin's "modest request" and the preceding requested letter are not identified as a surviving text.

incoming_reviews.summary: Fanny writes at her father's request about his trip to London/Haleybury and Arthur's scrapes, and asks about Darwin's horses and partridges. No direct Darwin reply is identified.
unlocated_references: The prior Darwin communication and any reply remain unlocated.

incoming_reviews.summary: Fanny sends Darwin a book through Francis, reports hunting and family activities, and promises another scrawl. Delivery of the book is a parcel/book channel rather than evidence of a letter prompt; no direct reply is assigned.
unlocated_references: The book Darwin requested and the prior promised exchange are not uniquely identified.

incoming_reviews.summary: Fanny requests oil color, brushes, and a book to be brought from Whitney's, with a Monday visit and an order for Halston. This is a practical request; no direct Darwin reply survives here.
unlocated_references: Darwin's preceding request or arrangement for the Monday visit is not identified.

incoming_reviews.summary: Charlotte congratulates Darwin after his fate is decided, discusses the delayed Henslow letter, FitzRoy, the added third year, family anxieties, and social plans. She says Elizabeth and she are going to the Bents at Derby for the music meeting next week and that a Welsh party heard intelligence about Darwin at Overton. These are social/contextual clues, not proof of a particular later Fox exchange.
unlocated_references: Charlotte's received Darwin letter and the delayed letter to Henslow are not themselves a surviving direct family target in this packet.

proposed_links.reason: The music-meeting statement is "Elizabeth & I are going next week to the Bent's at Derby for the music meeting" (DCP-LETT-133 P1), while DCP-LETT-149 only says Darwin heard of Fox at the Music Meeting and sat by Charlotte. The event/topic overlap does not identify Charlotte's letter as a source of the Fox report or prove the channel/timing.

incoming_reviews.summary: Fanny sends a small purse as a keepsake and asks Darwin to remember Charles Mogg. No direct Darwin reply is assigned.
unlocated_references: No preceding or subsequent Darwin response is identified.

incoming_reviews.summary: Fanny regrets missing Darwin before his departure, asks for his plans and a final farewell, and supplies extensive Devonshire, family, debt, horse, and cabin-related social commentary. She requests that the letter be burned; no reply is preserved in this family assignment.
unlocated_references: Caroline's informing letter and the requested final Darwin farewell are not recovered as texts.

incoming_reviews.summary: Sarah encloses a promised hair pin, reflects on Darwin's departure and Woodhouse, promises a future account, and refers to a short reprieve/delay for his family. No direct Darwin reply is assigned.
unlocated_references: The specific Darwin departure communication and the source of the short-reprieve information are not identified.

incoming_reviews.summary: Fanny says their letters crossed, quotes Darwin's concern about being forgotten, discusses the three-year absence and his sailing date, and asks for another letter if possible. The crossed Darwin letter is not among this family's outgoing records, and no further direct reply is present.
unlocated_references: The Darwin letter received a few days earlier and the exact crossing/dispatch sequence are unlocated.

incoming_reviews.summary: Fanny relies on Catherine's report that Darwin remained in suspense at Plymouth, then gives a long account of Sarah's wedding and asks for a final adieu. This is postdating every family outgoing target and should not be activated as a pre-target prompt.
unlocated_references: Catherine's letter reporting Plymouth status is referenced but not identified; Darwin's requested final adieu is not recovered.

findings.finding: Family/social incoming letters are evidence of possible correspondence context, not proof of Darwin's reading. Mostyn/Owen letters 37-44, 51, 77, 83, 85, 97, 134, 136, 137, 141 and 151 have no surviving direct Darwin target in this assignment; they remain incoming voices and must not be promoted merely because they were sent.

DCP-LETT-115's held Henslow letter is unresolved: P4 says Susan may open it, while P1 says Darwin heard only part of FitzRoy's letter through Wood. Candidate DCP-LETT-105 is therefore physical possession/possible reading context, not activated knowledge.

DCP-LETT-115 and 117 form a likely draft/revision or continuation sequence because 117 P1 says "bringing up the other with me & altering it"; neither text proves that 115 was mailed or received by Susan. DCP-LETT-122's "letter written next day" is likewise a candidate reference to 119, not a guaranteed identity.

DCP-LETT-145 contains two distinct incoming family inputs: Caroline's letter was received the same day Darwin wrote to Susan, then a Catherine letter arrived. The questioned date [31?] October and crossed/uncertain channels must remain explicit. DCP-LETT-146 confirms a Susan-dated communication but not a new Caroline letter.
DCP-LETT-133's Derby music-meeting plans do not identify the report in DCP-LETT-149 that Darwin heard of Fox at the Music Meeting; shared event vocabulary is insufficient for a knowledge link.

DCP-LETT-49 is the clearest family-group incoming relation: a Herbert letter was received late and answered. The two Whitley admonitions and Darwin's answer are separately narrated and remain unlocated rather than being collapsed into a surviving record.

limitations: The review establishes paragraph coverage and exact textual evidence only within the supplied packet and cross-group source packet; absence from the selected corpus is not proof that a letter never existed.
Incoming records do not by themselves establish physical receipt or reading by Darwin; where no outgoing acknowledgment exists, the review reports the text and leaves the target unlocated.
Date ranges, questioned dates, and composition-versus-dispatch distinctions are retained from the packet; no CSV sorting date was treated as an exact event date.
DCP-LETT-151 is postdated relative to all assigned outgoing targets and was kept as contextual incoming evidence only, with no pre-target activation.
